name: Deerhunter
label: 4AD
lede: Bradford Cox started Deerhunter in Atlanta under a name he hated, lost his bassist in 2004 and watched fans download his records before he could release them. By Halcyon Digest it was the indie band a lot of people name first.

eras.title: A throwaway name and a lost bassist
eras.text: Bradford Cox figured Deerhunter was a temporary art project when he started it in Atlanta. The bassist died just as it turned into a band, and the debut came out of that.

years.h: Bradford Cox and Moses Archuleta start a band in Atlanta
years.p: Their first drummer, Dan Walton, picks the name Deerhunter. Cox, living alone in a big suburban house after his parents divorced, thought the band was a temporary art project and has said he despised the name.
years.xp:
Cox was born with Marfan syndrome, which by age ten had started to change how he looked, and he dropped out of high school and later earned a GED. He met guitarist Colin Mee at Die Slaughterhaus Records, and they bonded over Dada, Messiaen, Ligeti, [[The Fall|d5da1841-9bc8-4813-9f89-11098090148e]], [[The Raincoats|42201355-08b7-43b6-a7b8-866f612e1600]] and Cabaret Voltaire.

Paul Harper played bass first; Justin Bosworth replaced him.

years.h: Justin Bosworth dies at 24 after a skateboarding fall
years.p: Head injuries kill the Deerhunter bassist on March 29, 2004. His only release with the band is a split with Alphabets, and the debut album's liner notes are dedicated to him.

q: I don't ever want to make this album again.
years.h: Debut Turn It Up Faggot arrives on Stickfigure
years.p: Josh Fauver of Electrosleep International plays bass. Bradford Cox calls the record the result of a lot of negativity, made in the year after Bosworth's death.

years.h: Childhood friend Lockett Pundt takes the second guitar
years.p: Pundt, who knows Bradford Cox from way back, becomes his songwriting partner and an occasional lead singer.

years.h: A Brooklyn studio, walking pneumonia and an untuned piano sink the second album
years.p: At Rare Book Room with Samara Lubelski, Bradford Cox has influenza and walking pneumonia, the piano is out of tune and the tape machine isn't calibrated.
years.xp:
Cox said he kept the failed sessions on a scratched CD-R under his bed that nobody would ever hear. Excerpts later went up as free downloads on the band's blog anyway.

The second album that did come out, Cryptograms, was recorded in two days in November 2005.

eras.title: Two Kranky records and a leak
eras.text: Chicago's Kranky put out the records that made Deerhunter a critics' band, while Cox blogged nonstop. Fans heard his music early whether he wanted them to or not.

years.h: Kranky puts out Cryptograms, and Pitchfork names it Best New Music
years.p: Cut in rural Georgia over two single-day sessions, the first ending as "Red Ink" spins the tape off the reel. It's dedicated to Bradley Ira Harris, a friend of Bradford Cox's who died in 2005 after heroin addiction.
years.xp:
Chris Bishop produced and engineered, at the same studio as the debut. The second half was recorded months later, in one day in November. Pitchfork put it 14th on its albums of 2007 list.

The record sounded quieter and more inward than the debut, and a year earlier Pitchfork had already put "Spring Hall Convert" in its Infinite Mix Tape series.

years.h: Fluorescent Grey adds bells, piano and keyboards
years.p: The Kranky EP is where Deerhunter starts layering in rudimentary keyboards, bells and piano.

years.h: Colin Mee quits over missed shows, and is back four months later
years.p: Mee says he couldn't make a couple of booked shows and that certain bandmates found that unacceptable.

years.big: "I did not react well to the leak, in retrospect."
years.h: Bradford Cox's solo album Logos leaks, unfinished
years.p: Cox on the August 2008 leak of his Atlas Sound record. Microcastle had already leaked in May.
years.xp: Cox went on to call the whole episode "the kind of internet-fueled drama that I was quickly learning to despise." It set up the scramble over Microcastle that fall.

years.h: Microcastle goes out, with a bonus record the leak forced
years.p: Recorded in a week at Rare Book Room with Nicolas Vernhes. Kranky rushes it out digitally on August 19 after the leak, and the band records a second album, Weird Era Cont., which leaks too.
years.xp: It's Deerhunter's first entry on the Billboard 200, at No. 123, and Wikipedia says it sold over 50,000 copies in the US. Lockett Pundt wrote "Agoraphobia," and [[Black Lips|e940d7a3-01d0-468c-86ea-5dc4d89dcf80]]' Cole Alexander added vocals to "Saved by Old Times" over iChat. Pitchfork gave it 9.2 and ranked it fifth of 2008.

years.h: Mee leaves for good, and a high-school friend takes his guitar
years.p: Whitney Petty, a former cheerleader who went to school with Bradford Cox, joins for tours as second guitarist.

years.h: Whitney Petty is out after months, and Deerhunter is four again
years.p: Bradford Cox posts on the band's blog that she's a "free spirit" and a great friend, and that Deerhunter is the four of them.

years.h: Rainwater Cassette Exchange collects Microcastle leftovers
years.p: The songs were written during the Microcastle sessions. That summer Deerhunter tours as the No Deachunter Tour with [[No Age|55821c25-bd47-4f67-baf8-17ccd2cf1c86]] and [[Dan Deacon|8dd73d1a-0424-4581-af8c-ade3edb44c5a]].

years.h: At All Tomorrow's Parties, Bradford Cox says it's the last show for a long time
years.p: He tells the crowd Deerhunter will take time for other things. Drummer Moses Archuleta enrolls in culinary school.

eras.title: Halcyon days on 4AD
eras.text: The hiatus lasted months, not years. Deerhunter moved to 4AD, made the album most people now name first, and lost its founding bassist by email.

years.cap: Deerhunter at the Ogden Theatre, Denver, April 2010
years.h: Halcyon Digest lands on 4AD, and Pitchfork ranks it third of 2010
years.p: A guerrilla campaign launches it, with "Revival" going to fans who helped promote it. AllMusic gives five stars; Pitchfork later puts it 29th of the 2010s.
years.xp: The saxophone on "Coronado" came from Bradford Cox playing the Rolling Stones' Exile on Main St. reissue on repeat. He predicted everyone would have saxophones on their records the next year.

years.cap: Cox, Fauver and Pundt at LouFest, St. Louis, August 2011
years.h: The bassist quits by email, just before the Monomania sessions
years.p: Josh Fauver is gone, and Josh McKay takes the bass. Atlanta's Frankie Broyles joins on guitar.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Fauver's 2012 departure put the band's future in doubt. Fauver had played on every record since the debut.

years.h: Network TV gets the title track a month early
years.p: Deerhunter plays "Monomania" on Late Night with Jimmy Fallon on April 2.

years.h: Monomania goes nocturnal, with rats and insects on tape
years.p: Recorded at Rare Book Room with Nicolas Vernhes, it uses treated recordings of rats and insects and deals with dissociation and mental illness. Josh McKay is on bass.
years.xp: The press release called the sound "nocturnal garage." The album was announced on March 22 for a May 7 release.

years.cap: Deerhunter at Primavera Sound, Barcelona, May 2011
years.h: Deerhunter curates ATP at a holiday camp and plays three albums in full
years.p: At Pontins in Camber Sands, the band headlines and plays Cryptograms, Microcastle and Halcyon Digest start to finish. Atlas Sound plays too.

eras.title: Hit by a car, then a slow fade
eras.text: A car hit Cox while he was walking his dog, and his recovery produced the band's warmest record. Four years later a former bassist died, and after one more album Deerhunter stopped.

years.h: A car hits Bradford Cox as he walks his dog
years.p: It happens near Grant Park in Atlanta. Cox is seriously injured and hospitalized, and writes songs through his rehabilitation.

years.cap: Deerhunter on the main stage at Field Day, London, June 2016
years.h: Recovery produces Fading Frontier
years.p: Before it comes "Snakeskin," with saxophonist Zumi Rosow in the video, and "Living My Life," dedicated to Miles Davis.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Bradford Cox focused on writing songs during his recovery and rehabilitation, and that the 4AD record was very well received by critics.

years.h: Double Dream of Spring exists only on cassette, sold on tour
years.p: It's a mostly instrumental album.

years.h: Josh Fauver, bassist on the first four albums, dies at 39
years.p: Deerhunter announces his death in Atlanta. No cause was given.

years.h: Cate Le Bon produces Why Hasn't Everything Already Disappeared?
years.p: The first single, "Death in Midsummer," had come out the previous October.

years.cap: Deerhunter at the Gothic Theatre, Englewood, Colorado, October 2016
years.h: Thirteen minutes, one take, straight to tape
years.p: "Timebends" is a partly improvised Halloween single, recorded live with almost no overdubs. After a European tour that November, Deerhunter goes quiet.

eras.title: Eight new songs in Philadelphia
eras.text: Deerhunter has been inactive since 2019. In 2026 Cox came back onstage alone.

years.h: Cox walks onstage alone in Philadelphia with eight new songs
years.p: At the Making Time festival, the set is described as largely soft and ruminative, with synth drones and echo-brushed vocals.
years.xp: Track names were handed out on set lists and lyric sheets to people in the audience.
